newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta stocks end down, tone cautious on rupiah.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta stocks end down, tone cautious on rupiah.

text.p: Jakarta stocks ended down on Monday as overall market sentiment remained cautious as regional currency volatility spilled over to the rupiah, brokers said.
The Jakarta composite index ended down 0.92 points, or 0.13 percent, at 722.50 points after touching a day low of 719.52 points. Decliners led advancers by 82 to 41 with 62 issues unchanged.
Total turn-over was estimated at 480 billion rupiah.
"Sentiment was cautious as players were watching the volatile rupiah," one broker said.
Bank dealers said the rupiah was trapped in a zone of turbulence and was sensitive to movements in the region.
Spot rupiah stabilised at around 2,450.0/55.0 at 0910 GMT.
The rupiah fell to an intra-day low of 2,469.0 from an opening of 2,453.0 before it bounced back to a high of 2,445 and settled at 2,455 at midday.
Most banking stocks closed lower due to the cautious sentiment on the rupiah, brokers said.
They added that reports of Moody's downgrading its ratings outlook on the seven state banks to uncertain from stable was seen further dampening sentiment on the sector.
Moody's Investors Service said on Monday it was revising its ratings outlook for Indonesia's state banks to uncertain from stable pending a decision on planned mergers among the seven state banks.
Bank BNI, the only state-owned listed bank fell 25 rupiah to 1,500 rupiah, with around six million shares traded due to the weak sentiment, brokers said.
"In the short term, the mergers will squeeze the profitability of the better-managed state banks like BNI," said Rajiv Louis, banking analyst with PT Schroders Indonesia, said.
Indonesia, however, is expected to weather the Asian currency storm with the backing of sound economic fundamentals and conservative fiscal management by the central bank, economic analysts said.

Brokers said the stock market composite index was likely to remain generally flat on Tuesday, but sentiment was seen remaining cautious as the local currency was seen remaining under attack from speculators.

Cement maker Indocement recorded further gains as it closed 175 rupiah higher at 4,550 rupiah in active trading on market talk that the firm planned to divest its stake in sister company noodle maker Indofood, brokers said.
